insight: There's been no measurable rain lately, so there's no runoff driving contamination, and strong summer sunlight is helping disinfect the water. The model's main signals right now: recent rainfall is raising risk by washing bacteria-laden runoff into the surf; hours since high tide is lowering risk — the timing relative to high tide affects how concentrated bacteria are at the shoreline; and wave period is lowering risk — longer-period swell reaches deeper and can resuspend sediment-bound bacteria. The last lab sample (51 MPN/100mL) is now 8 days old — beaches are sampled about weekly, so a reading this stale carries little weight, and this estimate leans on current conditions. It's a naturally clean, well-flushed open-coast beach (unsafe only ~3% of the time), so outside of storms it's reliably safe.
